title: etwdump: Fix out-of-bounds access parsing LDAP ETW messages
description:
etw_dump_write_ldap_event() allocates the "Message" property at exactly
the size reported by TdhGetPropertySize(), then treats it as a
NUL-terminated hexdump line that is at least 48 bytes long:

 - the strncmp() prefix checks read up to 11 bytes from a buffer that
   may be shorter,
 - the decode loop reads Message[i * 3] up to offset 45 without
   checking Length,
 - sscanf() scans forward from a buffer that need not be terminated,
 - the decoded bytes are written back into the same allocation at
   Message[i] for up to 16 iterations, which is out of bounds when
   Length < 16.

A crafted ETL file with a short LDAP "Message" property triggers the
out-of-bounds read, and depending on the heap contents the in-place
decode can also write past the allocation.

This is reachable with well-formed input too: a valid trailing hexdump
line such as "41 42" gives Length == 6, and the loop reads Message[6],
one past the end. sscanf() then fails and the already decoded bytes are
discarded, so short final lines were also being dropped from the
reassembled buffer.

Bound every access by Length, use memcmp() for the prefix checks, and
decode into a local buffer with g_ascii_xdigit_value() instead of
overwriting the property allocation. Also reject a zero-length property
before g_malloc(), since g_malloc(0) returns NULL.

Reported by Aisle Research.

Fixes #21489

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ronnie Sahlberg <ronniesahlberg@gmail.com>

notes.body:
It is an obscure file format for Windows and it is unclear how exploitable it is.
Regardless, any attack likely involves asking the end user to "download this file and load into wireshark" so ...

I don't think it justifies backporting to other stable branches and master should be sufficient.
